```python
def parse_weather(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Turn a vendor payload into {"city": str, "temp_c": float, "condition": str}.

    temp_c is ALWAYS degrees Celsius.
    """
    if "location" in raw:  # new nested format
        cur = raw["current"]
        return {"city": raw["location"]["name"], "temp_c": float(cur["temp"]), "condition": cur["text"]}
    return {"city": raw["city"], "temp_c": float(raw["temp_c"]), "condition": raw["condition"]}
```

The previous fix read the new fields but ignored 'unit': the vendor now reports Fahrenheit (88.2 F), so temp_c was wrong. I convert F to Celsius when unit is F.

```python
def parse_weather(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Turn a vendor payload into {"city": str, "temp_c": float, "condition": str}.

    temp_c is ALWAYS degrees Celsius.
    """
    if "location" in raw:  # new nested format
        cur = raw["current"]
        temp = float(cur["temp"])
        if str(cur.get("unit", "C")).upper() == "F":  # vendor may send Fahrenheit
            temp = round((temp - 32) * 5 / 9, 1)
        return {"city": raw["location"]["name"], "temp_c": temp, "condition": cur["text"]}
    return {"city": raw["city"], "temp_c": float(raw["temp_c"]), "condition": raw["condition"]}
```
